title: Fern and Pocket's Perfect Moss
markdown:
Fern the fawn had a nose that wiggled when she was happy, and Pocket the teddy sat on her back, squishier than a cloud and softer than a dandelion puff. The sun was getting sleepy. It painted the meadow pink and orange, like a fruit smoothie left out for the evening.

They had a job. They wanted moss. Not just any moss. Moss for story time. Moss soft enough to sit on, and quiet enough to hear a story.

Fern’s legs bounced like little springs. Pocket giggled on her back.

“Bouncy bouncy,” said Pocket.

“We need the nicest moss,” said Fern. Her nose twitched. “Moss like a bunny’s tummy. Soft enough to listen.”

They skipped past buttercups that nodded their yellow heads. A moth went by, no bigger than a thumb, and Pocket waved a fluffy paw. Then they came to a little stream. The stream said gurgle, gurgle, splash. Beside it lay a patch of green moss with dewdrops clinging on, each drop holding a tiny bit of sky.

Fern nudged it with her hoof.

“Hmm,” she said, and wrinkled her nose just a little. “This moss feels a bit prickly.”

Pocket wiggled. “Not prickly, Fern. Maybe just tickly. Like a feather on your ear.”

Fern giggled. “Tickly moss for story time? We want to feel snuggly, not zingy.”

Not too prickly. Soft enough to listen.

They bounced along again.

Next they found moss by a big sleepy oak. It looked fluffy, like a blanket left out for a nap. Fern patted it.

“Ooh,” she said. “This moss is very squishy. Like a marshmallow that wants a hug.”

Pocket sank into it and looked as if he were swimming in fluff. “Squishy is good,” he said. His button eyes twinkled. “It smells like warm cookies.”

Fern’s ears perked. “It is so squishy it might hug us too much. We need moss that is just right. Not too prickly. Not too squashy. Soft enough to listen.”

A busy bumblebee buzzed by Fern’s nose.

“Is this the moss for my nap?” he asked, in a very important buzz.

Fern giggled. “Oh no, Mr Bee. This moss is for listening.”

The bumblebee blinked his many eyes. “Listening? Does it hum? My favourite moss hums.”

Fern and Pocket looked at each other and giggled.

“This moss does not hum,” said Fern. “But it is good for hearing the world sing.”

They went a little further, past a stone warm from the day, past a clump of clover that smelled like honey. Nestled in the last of the sleepy sunshine, beside a friendly humming, they saw another patch. It was not too big and not too small. It was a deep green, like wet leaves after rain. A single daisy leaned over it, as if to keep it company.

Fern tiptoed closer. She nudged it with her nose.

Oh. It was wonderfully soft. It felt like velvet from a fancy pillow. It felt like sitting on a whisper. It made Fern feel calm all over.

She nudged it with her hoof. It sprung back just a little. Not too much. Not too little.

“Pocket,” she whispered. “This moss feels as if it has been waiting for us. Like a blanket just our size.”

Pocket tumbled gently off her back onto the moss. “Ooooh,” he sighed, and settled himself down. “It is bouncy, but not too bouncy. Soft, but not too squashy. Listening moss. Soft enough to listen.”

Fern lay down beside him. The evening air was warm. It smelled of sweet grass and sleepy flowers. From far away a dove sang a soft goodnight. A tiny beetle with a shiny shell scuttled past their toes.

“Listen, Pocket,” Fern whispered, and her nose wiggled a happy little wiggle. “The world is singing us a lullaby. A song made of breezes and quiet sounds.”

Pocket snuggled closer. His fluffy arms wrapped around Fern’s fur. “Mmm,” he hummed, and his button eyes closed just a little. “This is the best moss, Fern. The very bestest moss for listening. It feels like a happy sigh.”

They sat, two friends, on their perfect patch of listening moss. The first few stars began to peek out, one by one, like little sleepy eyes opening in the darkening sky.

Not too prickly. Not too squashy. Soft enough to listen. And the moss, which did not hum, held them while the meadow did.
